title: New Gas Stations, Food Safety & Utility Upgrades
summary:
*   University students called for enhanced food safety, requesting stricter inspections of eateries near campus, which the Mayor agreed the City would fully support.
*   Two new drive-in gasoline filling stations were approved for construction at key intersections, signaling the city's expansion and growing infrastructure for motorists.
*   Significant utility upgrades were greenlit, allowing Southwestern Bell to install underground telephone conduits and Texas Public Service Company to lay new gas mains across various city streets.
*   A property owner sought to rezone land on West Sixth Street from residential to commercial, with the request referred for further review, indicating ongoing shifts in urban development.

REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL:
459
Austin, Texas, October 07, 1937..
The meeting was called to order at 11:00 A. M., with Mayor Tom Miller presiding. Roll call
showed the following members present: Councilmen C. M. Bartholomew, Simon Gillis, and
Mayor Tom Miller, 3; absent, Councilmen C. F. Alford and Oswald G. Wolf, 2.
The reading of the Minutes was dispensed with.
A committee of University of Texas students, sponsored by the Editor of the Daily Texan
and the President of the Students Association, petitioned the City Counc11 for a more
rigid inspection of all food establishments in the neighborhood of the University. The
Mayor advised the Committee that the City would cooperate to the fullest extent in the
matter.
C. M. Cassidy submitted a request that provision be made in the new pure food ordinance
for a more rigid inspection of plumbing in all food establishments. The matter was taken
under advisement.
